cite_as: Kraft, M. A., Edwards, D. S., & Cannata, M. (2024). The Scaling Dynamics and Causal Effects of a District-Operated Tutoring Program. EdWorkingPaper 24-1030 (Metro Nashville Public Schools).

Outcome: no average effect on math test scores; reading 0.04 to 0.09 SD. Tutors shifted from volunteers to teachers; sessions included before and after school.

cite_as: Carbonari, M. V., DeArmond, M., Dewey, D., Dizon-Ross, E., et al. (2026). Impacts of Academic Recovery Interventions on Student Achievement in 2022 to 2023. Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis.
claimed_component: Design: value-added models across 8 districts, 12 math programs. Outcome: robust positive effects in only five subject-intervention pairs, including one subject-specific tutoring program (+0.22 SD math); most programs served fewer students and lower dosage than planned; after-school arms not robust.

cite_as: Ritter, G. W., Barnett, J. H., Denny, G. S., & Albin, G. R. (2009). The Effectiveness of Volunteer Tutoring Programs for Elementary and Middle School Students: A Meta-Analysis. Review of Educational Research, 79(1), 3-38.
claimed_component: Design: meta-analysis of 21 randomized field trials of volunteer tutoring, grades K-8, United States. Confirm whether the pooled effect on math outcomes was statistically significant (expected: not significant), and the reading subskill effects.

cite_as: Parker, D. C., Nelson, P. M., Zaslofsky, A. F., Kanive, R., Foegen, A., Kaiser, P., & Heisted, D. (2019). Evaluation of a Math Intervention Program Implemented with Community Support. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 12(3), 391-412.
claimed_component: Design: student-level RCT, grades 4-8, n = 550, Minnesota Math Corps delivered by AmeriCorps members. Outcome: broad-based math assessment (STAR Math); intent-to-treat d = 0.17, d = 0.24 under optimal dosage.

cite_as: Codding, R. S., Nelson, P. M., Parker, D. C., Edmunds, R., & Klaft, J. (2022). Examining the impact of a tutoring program implemented with community support on math proficiency and growth. Journal of School Psychology, 90, 82-93.
claimed_component: Design: RCT of Math Corps (AmeriCorps tutors) rated Meets WWC standards without reservations. Outcome: STAR Math g = 0.17, statistically significant. Confirm grades and whether a state test was measured.

cite_as: ServeMinnesota (2018). A year-long state-wide RCT of the Minnesota Math Corps: Final report to Laura and John Arnold Foundation.
claimed_component: Design: statewide RCT. Outcomes: STAR Math g = 0.22 (significant) and Minnesota Comprehensive Assessment (state math test) g = 0.06 (not significant), per WWC study review.

cite_as: Robles, S., O'Connell, K., Gothro, A., et al. (2023). Math Corps' Tutoring Program: Math Knowledge Impacts and Participant Math Perceptions. Mathematica (ERIC ED628647).
claimed_component: Design: regression-adjusted matched comparison, grades 4-8. Model: AmeriCorps tutors, pairs or groups of three, 90 minutes a week in 30- to 45-minute sessions, scripted curriculum. Confirm the direction and size of the math impact and the test used.

cite_as: GO Tutor Corps Research Team (2025). Evaluation of High-Impact Math Tutoring Program: Impact on Student Gains (Evidence for ESSA record).
claimed_component: Design: quasi-experimental analysis, Stamford Public Schools, grades 6-10. Outcome: Evidence for ESSA rating Promising, mean effect +0.10. Confirm the test and the comparison group.

cite_as: Gersten, R., Rolfhus, E., Clarke, B., Decker, L. E., Wilkins, C., & Dimino, J. (2015). Intervention for First Graders With Limited Number Knowledge: Large-Scale Replication of a Randomized Controlled Trial. American Educational Research Journal, 52(3), 516-546.
claimed_component: Design: scale-up replication RCT of Number Rockets, 76 schools in four urban districts, 994 at-risk first graders, about 30 hours of small-group work. Outcome: significantly better on a broad standardized math measure (TEMA-3); effect size about 0.34 per Evidence for ESSA.

cite_as: Clarke, B., Doabler, C. T., et al. (2014, 2020). ROOTS / Whole Number Foundations Tier 2 mathematics intervention studies (Evidence for ESSA program record).
claimed_component: Design: five qualifying randomized studies of small-group Tier 2 math for kindergarten and grade 1, delivered by interventionists including paraprofessionals. Outcome: Evidence for ESSA mean effect +0.19 (Strong).

cite_as: Fuchs, L. S., Powell, S. R., Seethaler, P. M., Cirino, P. T., Fletcher, J. M., Fuchs, D., & Hamlett, C. L. (2010). Learning and Individual Differences, 20(2), 89-100 (Pirate Math).
claimed_component: Design: randomized study of one-to-one Pirate Math tutoring for low-achieving grade 3 students (Nashville and Houston). Outcome: KeyMath effect size +0.37 per Evidence for ESSA (Promising).

cite_as: Fuchs, L. S., Schumacher, R. F., Long, J., Namkung, J., Malone, A. S., et al. (2016). Effects of intervention to improve at-risk fourth graders' understanding, calculations, and word problems with fractions. Elementary School Journal, 116(4), 625-651 (Fraction Face-Off!).
claimed_component: Design: RCTs of small-group fraction tutoring for at-risk grade 4 students in Nashville (12 weeks). Outcome: Evidence for ESSA mean effect +0.51 on the qualifying (non-researcher) measure; confirm which measure qualified.

cite_as: Dietrichson, J., Filges, T., Seerup, J. K., Klokker, R. H., Viinholt, B. C. A., Bøg, M., & Eiberg, M. (2021). Targeted school-based interventions for improving reading and mathematics for students with or at risk of academic difficulties in Grades K-6. Campbell Systematic Reviews, 17(2), e1152.
claimed_component: Design: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs and QEs, grades K-6. Outcome: pooled effect on standardized reading and math tests; confirm that tutoring and small-group instruction had among the largest effects and the size for math.

cite_as: Dietrichson, J., Bøg, M., Filges, T., & Klint Jørgensen, A.-M. (2017). Academic Interventions for Elementary and Middle School Students With Low Socioeconomic Status: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Review of Educational Research, 87(2), 243-282.
claimed_component: Design: meta-analysis of RCTs and QEs for low-SES students, OECD countries. Outcome: standardized reading and math tests; confirm tutoring had among the largest pooled effects and its size.

cite_as: Bhatt, M. P., Guryan, J., Khan, S. A., LaForest-Tucker, M., & Mishra, B. (2024). Can Technology Facilitate Scale? Evidence from a Randomized Evaluation of High Dosage Tutoring. NBER Working Paper 32510.
claimed_component: Design: RCT, about 4,000 students in two large districts (grades 9-10). Model: in-school groups of four, two with an in-person tutor and two on computer-assisted learning, alternating daily, about 30% cheaper per pupil than 2-to-1. Outcome: 0.23 SD on math standardized tests for participants.

cite_as: Evidence for ESSA (Johns Hopkins CRRE). Saga Math program record (three RCTs: Guryan et al. 2023; Bhatt et al. 2024).
claimed_component: Rating Strong; mean effect size +0.14 across three qualifying RCTs with over 6,000 grade 9-10 students. Confirm whether +0.14 is an intent-to-treat estimate.

cite_as: Dietrichson, J., Filges, T., Klokker, R. H., Viinholt, B. C. A., Bøg, M., & Jensen, U. H. (2020). Targeted school-based interventions for improving reading and mathematics for students with, or at risk of, academic difficulties in Grades 7-12. Campbell Systematic Reviews, 16(2), e1081.
claimed_component: Design: meta-analysis of RCTs and QEs, grades 7-12. Outcome: standardized reading and math tests; confirm the pooled effect and whether small-group instruction or tutoring had the largest effects.

cite_as: Kraft, M. A. (2015). How to Make Additional Time Matter: Integrating Individualized Tutorials into an Extended Day. Education Finance and Policy, 10(1), 81-116.
claimed_component: Design: two quasi-experimental methods (unanticipated implementation and admissions lottery) at MATCH Charter Public High School. Outcome: daily tutorials by full-time recent graduates raised grade 10 ELA by 0.15-0.25 SD a year; no average effect in mathematics (gains only at the low end by quantile regression).

cite_as: Snipes, J., Huang, C.-W., Jaquet, K., & Finkelstein, N. (2015). The effects of the Elevate Math summer program on math achievement and algebra readiness (REL 2015-096). IES, REL West.
claimed_component: Design: RCT of rising grade 8 students, Silicon Valley districts, summer 2014, program run with the Silicon Valley Education Foundation (nonprofit). Outcome: MDTP Algebra Readiness test g about 0.64-0.66 (WWC); share algebra-ready rose from about 12% to 29%. Confirm program length and that no later state test or course outcome was measured.

cite_as: Lynch, K., An, L., & Mancenido, Z. (2023). The Impact of Summer Programs on Student Mathematics Achievement: A Meta-Analysis. Review of Educational Research, 93(2).
claimed_component: Design: meta-analysis of 37 experimental and quasi-experimental studies, pre-K-12. Outcome: average weighted impact +0.10 SD on mathematics achievement; similar in higher- and lower-poverty settings. Confirm the share of outcomes that were state tests and the timing of measurement (end of summer vs spring).

cite_as: Somers, M.-A., Welbeck, R., Grossman, J. B., & Gooden, S. (2015). An Analysis of the Effects of an Academic Summer Program for Middle School Students. MDRC.
claimed_component: Design: RCT of BELL's five-week middle school summer program (rising grades 6-8). Outcome: GMADE math g = 0.06, not statistically significant (about one month of learning, described as preliminary); GRADE reading g = 0.01.

cite_as: Lynch, K., & Kim, J. S. (2017). Effects of a Summer Mathematics Intervention for Low-Income Children: A Randomized Experiment. Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis, 39(1), 31-53.
claimed_component: Design: RCT, grades 3-9, N = 263, high-poverty urban district; offer of an online summer math program, with or without a free laptop. Outcome: treatment and control performed similarly on distal achievement measures.

cite_as: Cooper, H., Charlton, K., Valentine, J. C., & Muhlenbruck, L. (2000). Making the Most of Summer School: A Meta-Analytic and Narrative Review. Monographs of the Society for Research in Child Development, 65(1).
claimed_component: Design: meta-analysis of 93 summer school evaluations (mixed designs). Outcome: positive average effect of remedial or accelerated summer programs; confirm the size for math and whether effects were smaller in randomized designs.

cite_as: School District of Philadelphia, Office of Research and Evaluation (2022). Fall 2021 Performance on the Star Assessments for Students who Attended 2021 Summer Programs offered by SDP (with addendum).
claimed_component: Confirm design (matched comparison or descriptive), and the direction and size of fall Star Math differences for summer attendees vs comparison students. Star is the district interim test, not the PSSA.

cite_as: Adachi, E., Rolfhus, E., & Barfield, D. (2018). Evaluation of Texas 21st Century Community Learning Centers: A Site-Level Approach. Policy Brief. Westat (ERIC ED624482).
claimed_component: Design: propensity score matching per center and grade, 779 Texas centers, 2012-13. Outcome: distribution of center effect sizes on STAAR Math and Reading centered near d = -0.02; median attendance effect d = 0.14.

cite_as: Arellano, B. D., Naftzger, N., Ramirez, B., & Sutter, A. (2020). 21st Century Community Learning Centers: Texas ACEs 2014-15 Through 2016-17 Evaluation Report. AIR for the Texas Education Agency.
claimed_component: Design: propensity score matching, participants by days attended vs matched nonparticipants, statewide Texas. Outcome: confirm the STAAR math impact estimates (size and direction) by dosage band; attendance gain of 0.3 to 1.4 percentage points pooled.

cite_as: American Institutes for Research (2020). 21st Century Community Learning Centers: Texas Afterschool Centers on Education 2017-18 Evaluation Report. Texas Education Agency.
claimed_component: Design: propensity score matching by attendance band (30-119, 120+ days). Outcome: STAAR math about 4 scale-score points higher only at 120+ days; mostly negative relationship with STAAR scores at lower dosage. Confirm statistical significance and standardized size.

cite_as: Vinson, M., Liu, F., & Lin, S. (2019). New Jersey 21st Century Community Learning Centers Year 5 Evaluation Report: Impact Data for 2016-17. American Institutes for Research.
claimed_component: Design: propensity score matching of participants (30+/45+/60+ days) vs nonparticipants and vs low attenders. Outcome: confirm math impacts by grade (expected mixed; high vs low attenders about 0.037 SD) and ELA mostly null.

cite_as: American Institutes for Research (2024). New Jersey 21st Century Community Learning Centers Year 4 Evaluation Report: Descriptive Data and Attendance Study for 2022-23.
claimed_component: Design: inverse probability of treatment weighting on prior-year outcomes. Outcome: confirm test-score results were null and the unexcused absence rate was about 0.4 percentage points lower.
